effect: The liver releases glucose from glycogen into the blood, and the explanation completes the feedback sequence by showing why glucagon release lessens as glucose rises.
reaction: The result was expected, but the feedback explanation made the sequence more meaningful.

mostWorthwhile.text: The muscle and liver response to insulin was most worthwhile because it connected one hormone to glucose uptake, storage and reduced stimulation of further insulin release.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate steps showing insulin and glucagon traveling through blood felt repetitive; neither showed the target tissue's response until the following step.

surprise.text: Nothing particularly surprising happened; the final explanation clarified that rising glucose reduces the stimulus for further glucagon release.

arbitrary.text: No combination felt arbitrary: each followed the stated meal-to-storage-and-release goal. The choices were all the only offered combinations, so I did not discover their compatibility myself.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter if it offered more meaningful choices. The feedback relationships were clear, but this chapter's single-option sequence was predictable.
